## PG&E Urges Customers to Prepare as Planned Public Safety Power Shutoff Approaches


October 14, 2026


*Approximately 88,000 Customers in 29 Counties Are Being Notified of the Shutoff, and Provided Resources for Information and Support*


OAKLAND, Calif.


, Oct. 14, 2026


/ PRNewswire


/ -- Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) continues to closely monitor a statewide fire weather system that could require a Public Safety Power Shutoff ( PSPS


) event beginning Wednesday evening, October 14. Approximately 88,000 customers across 29 counties are currently in scope for the event. Customers have received multiple notices, and PG&E will notify customers again within four hours of their planned power shutoff.


**Stay Safe and Prepare Now**


PG&E encourages customers who have been notified to prepare themselves, their families and their homes for extended outages by:


- Charging phones, medical equipment and other essential devices.
- Having flashlights and fresh batteries available. Avoid using candles because of the fire risk.
- Keeping a supply of drinking water, nonperishable food and necessary medications available.
- Planning for medical needs or other needs that rely on electricity.
- Using generators safely. Never operate a generator indoors or in an enclosed space.
- Treating all electrical lines as energized and dangerous. Stay away from downed or damaged power lines and call 911 immediately to report them.
- Checking on family members, friends and neighbors who may need additional assistance.


Customers can check whether their address is currently in scope and get the latest PSPS


information at **pge .com/ PSPSupdates .**


**Support Is Available**


**Customers who may need additional support should contact 211 now.** Assistance is available before, during and after an outage, including support for customers who rely on power for medical needs or have other needs. Customers can call 211, text **" PSPS " to 211** or visit[211.org](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4798508-1&h=3541362818&u=https%3A%2F%2F211.org%2F&a=211.org) to get connected with available resources.


PG&E is also planning to open **more than 40 Community Resource Centers across 25 counties** during the potential PSPS


event. The centers offer ADA-accessible restrooms, device charging, Wi


- Fi


, blankets, air conditioning, bottled water, snacks and other supplies. Customers can find the nearest location through the[PG&E Outage Center – Ways We Can Help](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4798508-1&h=327946434&u=https%3A%2F%2Fpgealerts.alerts.pge.com%2Fways-we-can-help%2F%23crc-table&a=PG%26E+Outage+Center+%E2%80%93+Ways+We+Can+Help) .


**Support for Medical Baseline Customers**


Approximately 5,500 Medical Baseline customers are included in the current scope. When possible, PG&E employees will conduct individual in-person visits to Medical Baseline customers who do not verify that they have received important safety communications, with a primary focus on customers who rely on electricity for critical life-sustaining equipment.


**Potentially Affected Counties**


Approximately **88,000 customers in 29 counties** , including approximately **5,500 Medical Baseline customers** , and six Tribes may be impacted by the potential PSPS
